description:
BAZINGA is a technology-driven team passionate about software development, space exploration, and innovation. We aim to turn NASA's open data into creative and impactful digital solutions.

We welcome developers, data analysts, designers, science enthusiasts, and creative thinkers. We value teamwork, curiosity, and a willingness to learn.

Let's build something extraordinary beyond Earth's limits!
summary: First on Mars is an educational 2D survival and planetary exploration simulator built in Unity, where players step into the role of an astronaut wearing NASA's Z-2 planetary suit prototype alongside an autonomous rover during a 5-sol mission on Mars. The project integrates live telemetry from NASA CCMC DONKI (coronal mass ejections CME and solar flares FLR) synced every 6 hours via GitHub Actions to drive realistic plasma storm fronts and radiation hazards. Inside the pressurized spacecraft and 3-room greenhouse, players operate stations inspired by real space engineering (Apollo LM-5, MOXIE, ECLSS/UPA, APH/Veggie/PONDS, InSight, and Phoenix ISRU) and complete MAHLI, SAM, and CheMin science mini-games linked to 12 real Curiosity rover records and photographs. Its goal is to make space weather mitigation and Mars exploration intuitive and scientifically grounded.
details:
First on Mars is a 2D educational game prototype for children ages 7–12. Players control an astronaut and take part in three core activities: exploring Mars and collecting samples, cultivating crops, and protecting a Martian base. These mechanics introduce the decisions and resource tradeoffs involved in a space mission through interactive play.

The game uses space-weather records from NASA’s CCMC DONKI catalog, including coronal mass ejections and solar flares. It analyzes event dates, CME speeds, flare classes, and durations over a seven-day period, then converts event frequency and severity into shorter in-game alerts. These are simplified gameplay events, not a forecast of Martian weather. The astronaut’s 2D design takes inspiration from NASA’s Z-2 spacesuit reference model.

The project was built with Unity 6 and C# scripts, using 2D visual assets. It aims to spark scientific curiosity and help young players explore the challenges of operating a base on Mars.
